notes.summary: Primary foundations audited: bounded BGL construction only; closed-base Darvas completion, Perron and endpoint results imported with their exact scope.
notes.detailedSummary: Records independently accessed primary sources, operator and unnormalized metric conventions, closed Kähler hypotheses, and the singular endpoint-velocity limitation. BGL Section 2.2 requires BMP and is not imported on the Hopf manifold. No A–H target result is a premise.
notes.text:
This is an imported-foundation and evidence note, not a new completion theorem. All subsequent claims keep dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π), d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(4π), genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives, and the original joint Perron boundary convention. No change to the original multiplier-ideal convention, ordinary order, or singularity-volume definitions is made.

The two primary PDFs were independently opened through the connected web tool. [Darvas, arXiv:1401.7318v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.7318) uses i∂bar∂ and the unnormalized integral metric. On a compact connected Kähler manifold, E² means full non-pluripolar mass and finite second moment. Theorems 6.1/9.2 give its complete NPC smooth-distance completion and unique Perron segments; Theorem 3.6 gives E² rooftops; Theorem 5.2/Corollary 5.4 give endpoint capacity and L¹ convergence; Theorem 4.3 gives zero ordinary-model projection for full mass. Section 2.2, (16)–(17), supplies bounded Dirichlet uniqueness. Formula (15) computes distance from velocity for smooth endpoints. Section 7 explicitly prevents its unrestricted use at singular endpoints. The inspected proof chain uses decreasing approximation, Lemmas 6.3–6.9, Proposition 6.11, Lemma 6.12, density, rooftop contraction and Lemma 9.4; the NPC proof imports [CC]. These are permitted closed-base foundations, including their attributed cited foundations, not new Hermitian assertions.

The printed Section 7 example uses a mean-zero Green potential g on a curve, κ+i∂bar∂g=δ_x, and u_0=max(g,0), u_1=0. Initial MA is supported on {g≤0}, where dot u_0=0, although the endpoints have positive distance. Thus the initial squared-velocity integral is zero and cannot compute that distance, even for these Lipschitz endpoints.

[Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, arXiv:2406.01090](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090), Section 2.1, (2.1)–(2.3), constructs bounded products by the multilinear smooth-correction polynomial. Proposition 2.1 gives bounded-on-set locality, compatibility and positivity. Its proof uses local closed approximations of smooth backgrounds and Bedford–Taylor locality. Section 2.2 explicitly assumes BMP; that global theorem is not imported on X. Only local bounded Bedford–Taylor products, decreasing continuity, plurifine locality, canonical recovery, and the standards explicitly permitted in the assignment are otherwise imported. No new Hopf, rough pullback, mass, stationarity, energy-threshold or saddle result is imported.

This is ordinary primary evidence, with no recursive certification of every reference. Source-access outputs are retained in sources/web_reading_primary_find.json and sources/web_reading_primary_passages_1.json through sources/web_reading_primary_passages_6.json; sources/README.md records URLs and locations. Direct PDF downloads failed because sandbox networking is disabled, as recorded in artifacts/acquisition_log.txt. Optional acquisition command: python fetch_sources.py. No other-worker or verifier history was consulted. The source facts above are the exact external proof premises used below.

notes.summary: A: actual nonproduct Hopf geometry; h is nonclosed, fiber mass is 2, total mass 2n; current-level basic positivity equivalence proved.
notes.detailedSummary: For n≥3, constructs the compact connected quotient and elliptic action, proves nonproduct topology, computes differential and fiber factors, and descends genuine basic representatives including poles. A distributional Schur-complement test proves reverse positivity without restricting singular currents to fibers.
notes.text:
Target A is reconstructed. Put n≥3, d=n−1, Y=P^d, and κ=dd^c log||z||², interpreted projectively; with the stated operator its projective mass is ∫Yκ^d=1. Write α=π*κ, r=log||z||² on the cover, β=dr∧d^cr, and h=α+β. Time parameters below are denoted t and are separate from r.

Multiplication by e acts freely and properly discontinuously on C^n\{0}; radial logarithm identifies the quotient smoothly with S^(2n−1)×(R/2Z). The closed radial annulus 1≤||z||≤e is a compact fundamental set, so X is an actual compact connected smooth complex n-fold. The map π:X→P^d is a holomorphic submersion: on each standard affine chart use a nonzero projective coordinate as the scalar coordinate. A fiber is C*/e^Z. The holomorphic action w·[z]=[e^w z] has kernel Z+2πiZ and hence defines the compact elliptic group E=C/(Z+2πiZ), freely and transitively on each fiber. This is not a product. Indeed H^(2k)(X,R)=0 for 1≤k≤n−1. A product of two positive-dimensional compact complex manifolds would have nonzero cohomology in the even degree equal to the real dimension of either factor, by pulling back its oriented top class. That degree is strictly between 0 and 2n. Thus X admits no such complex product decomposition; in particular X≠Y×E.

Scalar multiplication shifts r by a real constant, so dr,d^cr,α,β all descend and are E-invariant. On the cover,

  α=dd^cr,  β=(i/(2π))∂r∧bar∂r,  β²=0,  α^(d+1)=0.

The positive form α has precisely the scalar complex direction as kernel, and β is positive on that direction. Consequently h is Hermitian. Direct exterior differentiation, using dd^c+d^cd=0 on forms, gives

  dh=−dr∧α,   d^cβ=−α∧d^cr,   dd^cβ=−α²,
  h^k=α^k+kβ∧α^(k−1),   dd^c(h^k)=−kα^(k+1)  (k≥1).

In particular h is genuinely nonclosed, dd^ch=−α²≠0 for d≥2, and dd^c(h^d)=0. It is a big background in the original sense, using ρ=0 and ε=1 with reference Hermitian form h.

For a fiber write its scalar as λ=e^(x+iy). Then r=2x+constant and d^cr=dy/(2π). Its periods are x∼x+1 and y∼y+2π. Thus β|E=dx∧dy/π and ∫Eβ=2. Fubini then gives ∫Xh^n=n∫Xβ∧α^d=2n. This is the actual fiber integral, with no volume normalization inserted.

Here is the necessary current-level positivity argument. In a local holomorphic submersion chart (y,w), possibly with a strip coordinate among the y variables, r_w≠0 and r is independent of the strip coordinate. For a base distribution V set A=κ+dd^cV on the base, with the corresponding pulled κ on a strip. The total current is π*A+β. For every smooth base (1,0) vector ξ choose its smooth lift Lξ=ξ−(∂r(ξ)/r_w)∂w. Then ∂r(Lξ)=0, so β(Lξ,overline{Lξ})=0. If π*A+β is positive, evaluation on these smooth vectors gives the nonnegative distribution π*(A(ξ,barξ)). Test this against a nonnegative compactly supported product density whose vertical integral is one. The result is positivity of A(ξ,barξ) on the base. Polarization/all ξ gives A≥0. Conversely A≥0 implies π*A+β≥0, by distributional pullback under a submersion and positivity of β. Equivalently the vertical Schur complement is exactly A, including its distribution coefficients. This tests the total current in open charts; it never restricts an arbitrary singular current to a fiber and never infers positivity merely by deleting β.

An E-invariant genuine quasi-psh function descends first as a locally integrable distribution in these charts. Its distribution is independent of w. The preceding argument recovers a κ-psh base distribution whenever it is h-psh. Canonical psh recovery produces a genuine base representative v; π*v and the original function have the same distribution and are both canonical, hence agree everywhere, including poles. Conversely π*v is canonical, E-invariant and h-psh whenever v is canonical κ-psh; local psh potentials on the base pull back as functions and their canonical representatives agree. The same argument applies to base times a strip. In the smooth case strict spatial positivity is equivalent to κ+dd^cv>0. Thus canonical basic potentials, and basic subgeodesics, are exactly these pullbacks.

The fiber and normalization algebra is also checked in check_formulas.py. Rerun: python check_formulas.py > artifacts/check_output.txt. Those checks supplement, and do not certify, this geometric proof.

notes.summary: B: canonical truncations give the actual unbounded mass formula without Hopf BMP; the full Perron envelope is basic and attains E² endpoints in L¹(X).
notes.detailedSummary: Proves bounded products through the smooth-correction polynomial, then reconstructs the unbounded measure by increasing canonical levels. Full competitor-family symmetry proves Perron commutation; temporal chords preserve joint boundary bounds. Fiber pushforward of the fixed smooth volume transfers base L¹ endpoint convergence. No product-capacity theorem is used.
notes.text:
Target B is reconstructed from n1–n2; in particular no BMP hypothesis on the Hopf manifold is added.

First let v be bounded and κ-psh. In a base coordinate chart κ=dd^cℓ with ℓ smooth, so ℓ+v is bounded psh locally. Approximate it on smaller charts by decreasing smooth psh functions. The ordinary bounded Bedford–Taylor construction and its decreasing continuity identify every pulled horizontal product with the pullback of the base product. Apply the bounded smooth-correction polynomial to h+dd^cπ*v=π*(κ+dd^cv)+β. Horizontal degree n=d+1 is zero and β²=0. Consequently the actual bounded product is

  (h+dd^cπ*v)^n = nβ∧π*(κ+dd^cv)^d.

This identity is about the correction polynomial, not a fictitious local potential for the nonclosed form h.

For arbitrary genuine v use its canonical cutoffs v_k=max(v,−k), so u_k=π*v_k=max(π*v,−k) exactly, including pole values. The preceding identity and plurifine locality give the exact finite-level identity

  1_{u>−k}(h+dd^cu_k)^n
    = nβ∧π*[1_{v>−k}(κ+dd^cv_k)^d].

The closed-base measures on the right increase to MAκ(v) and have total mass at most one. Define β∧π*µ for a base measure µ by the positive measure whose integral of a nonnegative Borel f is ∫Y(∫_{π^−1(y)} fβ) dµ(y). This definition also follows from the bounded identities; the horizontal/cross terms of β drop against full base degree. It is consistent on overlapping charts. Its mass is 2µ(Y). Therefore the finite-level Hopf measures increase, with mass bounded by 2n, and define an actual finite non-pluripolar product without using any global nonclosed theorem. Their limit is

  MA_ext,h(π*v)=nβ∧π*MAκ(v).

It agrees with every canonical finite-level identity. Each finite-level measure is a restriction of a bounded smooth-correction product and therefore gives zero mass to every pluripolar set, by n1. Since these measures increase setwise, their limit has the same property: for any fixed pluripolar set Z its mass is sup_k µ_k(Z)=0. In particular no mass is assigned to the whole pole set. This establishes actual non-pluripolarity on X without any theorem about arbitrary rough pullback currents.

For every nonnegative Borel F on Y, including infinite integrals, Tonelli and ∫Eβ=2 give

  ∫X(π*F) MA_ext,h(π*v) = 2n∫Y F MAκ(v).

Here is the proof for ALL Hermitian Perron competitors. For every competitor W(x,s), temporal convexity holds at each fixed x, allowing the identically−∞ case. Indeed locally add a smooth p(x) with dd^cp≥h, independent of s. Then W+p is psh and its restrictions as functions to temporal complex lines are subharmonic or identically−∞; invariance in Im s gives convexity. Joint boundary bounds imply

  W_t(x)≤(1−t)u_0(x)+t u_1(x).

In particular the whole family is locally uniformly bounded above. Suppose the base family is nonempty. Its pullbacks are competitors by n2, so the full envelope is not identically−∞. Upper-envelope stability gives a canonical h-subgeodesic H. For every g∈E, W∘g is a competitor with the same joint boundary bounds. The FULL family is therefore permuted by E, and its supremum and usc regularization are E-invariant. By n2, H=π*V for a base κ-subgeodesic V. The displayed chord bound survives usc regularization, since its right side is usc. At either boundary it implies the required joint upper bound, including −∞ poles: near a pole the corresponding endpoint is smaller than every −K, while the other endpoint has a fixed finite upper bound. Hence V is in the original base Perron family. It is no larger than its envelope. The converse inequality follows from pulling back every base competitor. Thus H is exactly the pullback of the base envelope. Open submersions also commute with usc regularization, so there is no representative ambiguity.

The printed base convention uses pointwise temporal upper bounds. The same temporal chord inequality and endpoint usc show that these bounds imply the original joint bounds. Conversely joint bounds imply pointwise ones. This verifies that the imported closed-base Perron segment uses the family required here, rather than silently changing the boundary convention.

For base E² endpoints, n1 supplies a nontrivial E² rooftop, hence a constant-in-time base competitor, and base Perron endpoint convergence in L¹ and capacity. For the fixed original smooth probability dV on X, the fiber pushforward π_*dV has a smooth positive density m(y)κ^d obtained by integrating dV over fibers; compactness makes m bounded above and below. Therefore

  ||π*(V_t−v_i)||_{L¹(X,dV)}
    =∫Y|V_t−v_i|mκ^d →0  as t→i, i=0,1.

This is genuine L¹ endpoint attainment on X for the canonical endpoints, with every prescribed pole retained. No claim of pointwise finite-energy endpoint convergence at every point, or of a product-capacity comparison, is used. This note is an analytical proof conditional only on n1's permitted foundations, not an exhaustive computational experiment.

notes.summary: C: complete B₂ metric on basic potentials, retaining constants; d_B=2π√(2n)d_D and its unique geodesics are full Hermitian Perron segments.
notes.detailedSummary: The bijection of smooth basic and base paths, with exact operator scaling, transfers the permitted closed-base completion to actual basic mass 2n and finite second moment. Points are genuine potentials, not models or types. No infimum over nonbasic paths defines this metric.
notes.text:
Target C is reconstructed on POTENTIALS, retaining constants. Let B∞={π*v: v smooth, κ+dd^cv>0}. Define d_B solely as the infimum of raw Hermitian L² lengths of smooth basic paths. Let B₂={π*v: v canonical κ-psh, MAκ(v)(Y)=1, ∫Y|v|²MAκ(v)<∞}. No quotient by constants, ordinary equivalence, or model projection is taken.

For every smooth basic path u_t=π*v_t, n3 gives

  ∫X dot u_t²(h+dd^cu_t)^n=2n∫Y dot v_t²(κ+dd^cv_t)^d.

Every smooth basic path corresponds to exactly one smooth strictly positive base path by n2. For f=v/(2π), κ+i∂bar∂f=κ+dd^cv and dot v=2π dot f. The primary Darvas metric has precisely the integral ∫Y dot f²(κ+i∂bar∂f)^d and no division by volume. Hence length, path infimum, and thereafter completion give the exact identity

  d_B(π*v,π*w)=2π√(2n) d_D(v/(2π),w/(2π)),

where d_D has background κ, not a rescaled κ. This is a bijection and a constant metric scaling on the entire smooth domains. Under it, full mass is unchanged and the finite second moment scales by (2π)^−2. Normalizing a potential by an additive constant does not affect finiteness, by |v+c|²≤2|v|²+2c² and finite mass. Thus n1's closed-base completion theorem identifies the completion exactly with B₂, as genuine representatives. The identification has neither additional completion points nor removed pole values.

By n3, the characterization can equivalently be made entirely on X among basic h-psh potentials:

  MA_ext,h(u)(X)=2n,  ∫X|u|² MA_ext,h(u)<∞.

The completed metric is complete and NPC, with unique constant-speed segments. The base segments supplied by n1 pull back, by n3, to exactly the FULL Hermitian Perron segments using all competitors. They attain both endpoints in the original L¹(X,dV) sense. They also attain them in d_B since they are metric segments. For any c the base translation v_t=v+tc is its Perron segment: adding tc to a constant-in-time base potential is a competitor and temporal convexity is the upper bound. Its completed distance is |c| on the mass-one base (initially from formula (15) at smooth endpoints and then from completion). Consequently d_B(u,u+c)=√(2n)|c|. In particular this formula holds for u=0.

This is a construction and proof using a closed-base foundation, not an imported nonclosed completion. It never takes an infimum over arbitrary nonbasic paths. A metric between projected singularity classes cannot be inferred from it; n7 explains the obstruction to that inference.

notes.summary: D: metric-speed action uniquely minimizes on the basic Perron segment; smooth basic Perron paths are stationary under every full-X variation.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves smooth metric speed through a short-geodesic barrier and formula (15) at smooth endpoints, retaining the o(δ) C¹ time remainder. Differentiates the full raw action and averages its actual differential under E to prove stationarity without dropping torsion. No full-X minimization is asserted.
notes.text:
Target D is reconstructed. On absolutely continuous curves γ:[0,1]→(B₂,d_B), define A_B(γ)=(1/2)∫₀¹|γ'|²dt, with metric speed and the value +∞ allowed. For endpoints p,q put D=d_B(p,q). Elementary metric absolute-continuity theory gives

  D≤∫₀¹|γ'|dt≤(∫₀¹|γ'|²dt)^(1/2).

Thus A_B≥D²/2. The unique constant-speed Perron metric segment from n4 realizes equality. Conversely equality forces constant speed D almost everywhere and length D. For each 0≤s≤t≤1 the length bound gives d_B(γ_s,γ_t)≤D(t−s); combining this with the endpoint triangle inequality forces equality on all subintervals. The path is the unique constant-speed segment. If D=0, equality instead forces the constant path. This proves uniqueness of the endpoint action minimizer.

To identify this action on smooth basic paths it remains to prove metric speed, rather than assume it from an infinite-dimensional formal Riemannian structure. Work on the base with our dd^c first. Fix a time t on a C¹ path v_t in the smooth strictly positive domain, with C¹ dependence in spatial C² norm. For δ→0 set a=v_t, b=v_(t+δ), Δ=b−a. Then Δ/δ→dot v_t in C², with time remainder o(δ). On the unit auxiliary interval s∈[0,1], the chord Q_s=a+sΔ has uniformly strictly positive spatial form. Its mixed spatial-temporal derivatives are O(|δ|). For a fixed sufficiently large K the function

  Q_s−Kδ²s(1−s)

is a strip subgeodesic: its temporal coefficient is positive 2Kδ² (up to the common strip factor 1/4), dominating the O(δ²) mixed Schur complement against a uniformly positive spatial inverse. It has the exact endpoints a,b. Temporal convexity gives the upper chord bound on their Perron segment G_s. Therefore

  Q_s−Kδ²s(1−s)≤G_s≤Q_s.

At the common smooth initial endpoint, one-sided convex derivatives satisfy

  Δ−Kδ²≤dot G_0≤Δ.

Formula (15), used ONLY for these smooth endpoints and converted from i∂bar∂ by f=v/(2π), gives

  d_base(a,b)²=∫Y(dot G_0)²(κ+dd^ca)^d.

Divide by δ² and use uniform convergence dot G_0/δ→dot v_t to obtain the metric derivative (also for δ<0 by reversing the segment):

  |v'|_base(t)²=∫Y dot v_t²(κ+dd^cv_t)^d.

For a smooth path this holds at every interior time and implies absolute continuity by the original path-length bound; compactness supplies a uniform speed bound. The endpoint Taylor expansion above is o(δ) under C¹; an O(δ²) time Taylor remainder would require C² and is not being assumed. The O(δ²) barrier comes from mixed derivatives of the endpoint difference, not from that time Taylor remainder.

Multiplying by 2n as in n4 proves |u'|_B²=∫X dot u²(h+dd^cu)^n on smooth basic paths. Consequently A_B=S_X there, where S_X is exactly the original one-half raw action. At arbitrary singular points A_B remains the metric-speed action; no universal endpoint-velocity formula is asserted.

For full-X stationarity of a SMOOTH basic Perron path with strictly positive spatial forms, first differentiate the ORIGINAL smooth action, allowing a smooth arbitrary full-X variation η with η_0=η_1=0:

  δS_X(u)[η]=∫₀¹∫X[dot u dotη ω_u^n
                  +(n/2)dot u² dd^cη∧ω_u^(n−1)]dt,
  ω_u=h+dd^cu.

This formula retains all torsion contributions; integrating its second term on a generic Hermitian manifold would generate them. Here use symmetry of the full action, not a dropped-term Euler equation. Every g∈E is a holomorphic diffeomorphism preserving h. Change of variables gives S_X(g*u)=S_X(u) for every smooth full-X path. At the E-fixed path u, its derivative therefore satisfies δS_X(u)[g*η]=δS_X(u)[η]. Haar averaging, valid for this continuous linear differential, gives δS_X(u)[η]=δS_X(u)[barη], where barη=∫E g*η dg is smooth and basic with zero endpoints. Since the spatial forms of u are uniformly positive, both the original and averaged variations are legitimate for sufficiently small parameter.

Write u=π*v and barη=π*ζ. The exact basic action identity gives δS_X(u)[barη]=2n δS_base(v)[ζ]. On the closed base set a_t=κ+dd^cv_t and f=dot v_t. Direct differentiation, time integration by parts, and spatial Stokes using da_t=0 give

  δS_base(v)[ζ]
    =−∫₀¹∫Y ζ[ddot v a_t^d−d df∧d^cf∧a_t^(d−1)]dt.

Indeed the time term contributes −ζ(ddot v a_t^d+d f dd^cf a_t^(d−1)); the spatial term contributes +(d/2)ζ dd^c(f²)a_t^(d−1), and dd^c(f²)=2f dd^cf+2df∧d^cf. Thus the first-derivative square remains. The smooth base Perron segment solves (κ+dd^cV)^(d+1)=0 by n1; its positive spatial block and strip Schur complement give exactly ddot v a_t^d=d df∧d^cf∧a_t^(d−1), with our operator. So δS_base=0, and averaging proves δS_X=0 under EVERY smooth full-X fixed-endpoint variation.

This proves stationarity, not full-X minimization. A_B's minimization domain is B₂. The saddle directions in n9 lie outside the basic path class. No Kähler energy primitive on X is introduced.

notes.summary: E: diagonal projective paths are spatially nonconstant full Hopf Perron segments, stationary under all variations, with the stated exact distance and action.
notes.detailedSummary: A holomorphic strip map produces the smooth rank-d homogeneous solution. Mass-one simplex moments give d_B²=2[(Σa_j)²+Σa_j²]/(n+1) and action half that value. For n=3 and (1,−1,0), squared distance is 1 and action 1/2.
notes.text:
Target E is reconstructed. Let a_0,…,a_(n−1) be arbitrary reals and let

  v_t([z])=log(Σ_j e^(ta_j)|z_j|²/Σ_j|z_j|²),  u_t=π*v_t.

The ratio is scalar-invariant and positive, so it is an actual global smooth potential on P^d for every real t, not a formula confined to an affine chart. On the base times the strip consider the holomorphic map

  F([z],s)=[e^(a_0s/2)z_0:…:e^(a_(n−1)s/2)z_(n−1)].

Adding a local Fubini–Study potential to the complexification V produces log Σ_j|e^(a_js/2)z_j|². Consequently κ+dd^cV=F*κ as a (1,1) form on the strip product, interpreted using local projective potentials. This is semipositive of rank d; its (d+1)st power is zero. Its spatial slices are the strictly positive forms F_t*κ. The path has its displayed smooth endpoints. The bounded closed-base Dirichlet uniqueness in n1 therefore identifies it as the base Perron segment. By n3 its pullback is the FULL Hopf Hermitian Perron segment with all competitors. By n2 its spatial Hopf forms are strictly positive, and by n5 it is stationary for the original raw action under all smooth full-X fixed-endpoint variations.

For exact constants write p_j=|z_j|²/Σ|z_l|². At the point F_t[z], the velocity of v_t is Σa_jp_j, and a_t^d=(F_t*κ)^d. Change variables by this projective automorphism. The moment vector p under κ^d has uniform probability measure on the (n−1)-simplex. The elementary projective simplex integral gives

  E[p_i²]=2/[n(n+1)],   E[p_ip_j]=1/[n(n+1)]  (i≠j).

Hence the base velocity square is independent of t and equals

  ∫Y dot v_t² a_t^d=[(Σa_j)²+Σa_j²]/[n(n+1)].

Multiplying by the exact factor 2n from n3–n5 gives

  |u'|_B²=d_B(u_0,u_1)²=2[(Σa_j)²+Σa_j²]/(n+1),
  S_X(u)=A_B(u)=[(Σa_j)²+Σa_j²]/(n+1).

If the a_j are not all equal then for every t>0 the values v_t at the coordinate points are ta_j, so the path is spatially nonconstant. For n=3 and (1,−1,0), squared distance is 1 and action is 1/2. This lives on the nonproduct, genuinely nonclosed X of n2. These constants use the original unnormalized raw metric and the original dd^c; there is no hidden factor 2 in the potential or measure.

The two simplex moment identities and this n=3 specialization are recorded by check_formulas.py; rerun python check_formulas.py > artifacts/check_output.txt. The proof itself is the projective pullback and exact moment computation, not the numerical check.

notes.summary: F: full ordinary projection commutes with pullback but is zero on B₂; Legendre commutes, with E² ray slices required for metric conclusions.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves projection commutation at finite ordinary-order constants before the usc limit. The metric cannot descend through model projection or ordinary equivalence. Both Legendre operations commute, but metric-action conclusions for rays require every finite slice to lie in E². No full-type volume or unrestricted stretching theorem follows.
notes.text:
Target F is reconstructed, with its negative and conditional conclusions intact.

For each finite real C let Q_X,C be the usc envelope of all h-psh w satisfying w≤0 and w≤π*v+C. This family is nonempty: π*v+K works for K≤C and K≤−sup v. It is uniformly bounded above. The two obstacles are E-invariant, so composition by every g∈E permutes the FULL competitor family. Its canonical envelope is thus basic. Since min(0,π*v+C) is usc, the envelope remains below both obstacles. By n2 it is π*q_C, where q_C is κ-psh and q_C≤min(0,v+C). Conversely every such base competitor pulls back. Therefore

  Q_X,C=π*Pκ(min(0,v+C)).

Taking the increasing union over C and then usc regularization, which commutes with the open submersion π, gives precisely

  P_h[π*v]=π*Pκ[v].

The finite-C argument is necessary: the final ordinary-model envelope need not itself retain the input ordinary type, so one cannot simply treat it as a same-type competitor. This proves commutation for full ordinary model projection with all Hopf competitors. It embeds the base ordinary models injectively as canonical basic ordinary models: if p=Pκ[p], then π*p=P_h[π*p]; injectivity follows from surjectivity of π and canonical equality.

For every v of full base mass, n1's closed-base Theorem 4.3 with smooth obstacle zero gives Pκ[v]=0. In particular every point of B₂ projects to the ordinary model zero on X. By n4, distinct basic potentials have positive distance; already d_B(0,c)=√(2n)|c| for c≠0 while both projections are zero. Thus d_B does not descend through this model projection. It also cannot itself descend to ordinary types because it distinguishes constant translates. This is compatible with the original affine maximum barriers for ordinary-equivalent endpoints: their Perron slices retain that same ordinary type, while the potential segment may be metrically nonconstant.

The measure formula in n3 computes only the ACTUAL mass of each basic representative. The lower and upper singularity volumes in the original task take infimum/supremum over the ENTIRE fixed ordinary type, including nonbasic representatives. Nothing here computes those quantities. In particular neither BMP for all bounded h-psh potentials nor positive lower mass for that full class has been proved or used.

Let Γ_τ be a base model test curve with the original normalization, concavity, decreasing property, cutoff c and −∞ extension. By the projection identity its pullback is a basic Hopf model test curve with precisely the same pointwise properties and pole values. Pointwise supremum/infimum commute with pullback, and usc regularization commutes because π is open. Thus both original Legendre operations commute exactly:

  (sup_{τ<c}(π*Γ_τ+tτ))* = π*(sup_{τ<c}(Γ_τ+tτ))*,

Write o=[1:0:…:0], ψ=log(Σ_{j=1}^d|z_j|²/Σ_{j=0}^d|z_j|²), and v_a=1−(1−ψ)^a for 0<a<1, assigning the genuine value −∞ at o. On the hyperplane z_0=0 this is smoothly zero; away from o the formula is smooth. Its supremum is zero.

Use the affine chart z_0=1 with w∈C^d, R=|w|, s=log R², L(s)=log(1+e^s), p=e^s/(1+e^s), and q=1−log p. Then ψ=log p=s−L(s), v_a=1−q^a, and κ+dd^cv_a=dd^cH(s), where H=L+1−q^a. Define

  A=a q^(a−1),   B=a(1−a)q^(a−2),   P=p+A(1−p).

Direct differentiation gives

  H'=P>0,
  H''=p(1−p)(1−A)+B(1−p)²>0,
  −dP/dq=p(1−A)+B(1−p).

Here 0<A≤a<1 and B>0. The radial Levi criterion follows directly from the complex Hessian: tangential eigenvalues of ∂bar∂H(log|w|²) are H'/R² with multiplicity d−1, and its radial eigenvalue is H''/R². Thus the displayed form is positive off o. Globally one can also write it as (1−A)κ+A dd^cs+B dψ∧d^cψ in this chart; both coefficients and all three terms are nonnegative.

There is no arbitrary value assigned at the pole. For each k the genuine bounded cutoff max(v_a,−k) has local psh potential max(H,L−k). It is equal to L−k near o, and the maximum of psh functions on the joining annulus. Outside the chart it is the maximum of smooth κ-psh potentials. The cutoff is thus genuinely κ-psh, and its decreasing, nonidentically−∞ limit is exactly v_a, whose canonical value at o is −∞. This proves global κ-pshness without treating a removed value as irrelevant.

With dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π), the exact radial determinant gives

  (dd^cH)^d=(d!/π^d)(H')^(d−1)H'' R^(−2d) dλ(w),

where dλ is ordinary Lebesgue measure on C^d. Polar integration has sphere area 2π^d/(d−1)! and ds=2dR/R. Therefore, with σ the normalized unit-sphere measure, the exact angular/radial disintegration is

  (dd^cH)^d = d P^(d−1)H'' ds dσ
             = d P^(d−1)[p(1−A)+B(1−p)] dq dσ,

the second expression having positive measure orientation as q increases from 1 to ∞. In particular the mass of the ball s<s_0 in the untruncated radial measure is P(s_0)^d−P(−∞)^d. For κ alone this gives L'(s_0)^d, fixing the projective probability normalization exactly.

To identify the ACTUAL non-pluripolar measure, apply bounded Bedford–Taylor products to the canonical cutoffs. Let Q_k=(1+k)^(1/a); then {v_a>−k} is q<Q_k. On that set the cutoff product is precisely the smooth radial measure above by locality. The interior constant region and the possible boundary-shell measure at q=Q_k are excluded by the strict superlevel set. The finite-level non-pluripolar mass is exactly

  ∫_{v_a>−k}(κ+dd^c max(v_a,−k))^d=1−P(Q_k)^d.

Indeed P(q)→1 as q↓1 and P(q)→0 as q→∞. The divisor z_0=0 is a smooth zero-mass hypersurface for these smooth local measures. Passing to the increasing canonical levels therefore gives actual full mass one, with no mass assigned to o. This is a computation of the specified canonical non-pluripolar product, not of a distributional wedge at the pole.

The exact second-moment integral is

  ∫Y|v_a|²MAκ(v_a)
    =∫₁^∞(q^a−1)² d P(q)^(d−1)
             [p(q)(1−A(q))+B(q)(1−p(q))] dq,
  p(q)=e^(1−q).

Near q=1 its integrand is finite and tends to zero. At infinity p is exponentially small, P∼a q^(a−1), and the measure density is asymptotic to d a^d(1−a)q^(d(a−1)−1). The moment density is therefore asymptotic, with its actual positive leading constant, to

  d a^d(1−a) q^((d+2)a−d−1).

The integral is finite if and only if a<d/(d+2). At equality the integral truncated at q=Q equals d a^d(1−a) log Q+O(1). The O(1) follows because the remaining power corrections from (q^a−1)² decay at least q^(−a), and corrections involving p are exponentially small times powers. Thus the critical divergence is logarithmic in q=1−log p, equivalently a log-log radial divergence. Above the threshold it has a power divergence. No factor 2 or π is omitted from the determinant or angular integral.

By n3 the actual Hopf pullback has mass 2n and second moment 2n times the displayed integral. By n4 it belongs to B₂ precisely for 0<a<d/(d+2), retaining its genuine −∞ pole along the WHOLE elliptic fiber π^−1(o). If 0<a<b<d/(d+2), then v_b≤v_a and v_a−v_b=q^b−q^a→∞. Target H is reconstructed for every real c≠0 and n≥3. The full Hopf Perron segment from 0 to c is u_t=ct: it is a genuine strip subgeodesic, while the temporal convexity argument of n3 bounds every full competitor by ct. This proves the FULL Perron identity independently of basic distance minimization.

The all-variation stationarity can also be checked directly. At u=ct, the original variation formula is

  δS_X[η]=∫₀¹∫X[c dotη h^n+(nc²/2)dd^cη∧h^(n−1)]dt.

The time term is zero by fixed endpoints. By n2, dd^c(h^(n−1))=0, so smooth Stokes makes the spatial term zero for every smooth full-X η. The stationarity is not merely in basic directions.

The full raw-action Hessian at this path is

  S_X''(0)[η,η]=∫₀¹∫X[dotη²h^n
      +2nc dotη dd^cη∧h^(n−1)
      +(n(n−1)c²/2)(dd^cη)²∧h^(n−2)]dt.

It is important that the middle term is retained. For a scalar-radius function f(t,r), periodic of period two in r, the exact spatial form and mass are

  h+dd^cf=(1+f_r)α+(1+f_rr)β,
  (h+dd^cf)^n=n(1+f_r)^d(1+f_rr)β∧α^d.

It is strictly positive exactly when both 1+f_r and 1+f_rr are positive. Integration over the phase circle and projective base gives ∫XG(r)β∧α^d=∫₀²G(r)dr. Therefore the ORIGINAL raw action in this radial path class is

  S_X(f)=(n/2)∫₀¹∫₀² f_t²(1+f_r)^d(1+f_rr)drdt.

Put f=ct+εη with η=0 at both temporal endpoints. Expanding to second order, the spatial periodic integrals of η_rη_rr vanish, and the space-time integral of η_tη_rr is −(1/2)[∫η_r²dr]₀¹=0. The Hessian becomes

  Q(η)=n∫₀¹∫₀²[η_t²+2dc η_tη_r
                       +(d(d−1)c²/2)η_r²]drdt
      =n∫₀¹∫₀²[(η_t+dcη_r)²−(d(d+1)c²/2)η_r²]drdt.

Here d denotes the integer n−1, not an exterior derivative. Consider the actual global smooth variations

  η_k(t,r)=sin(πt)cos(kπ(r−dc t)),  k=1,2,….

They descend because r is a globally defined R/2Z coordinate and k is integral; their endpoints vanish. They satisfy (∂t+dc∂r)η_k=πcos(πt)cos(kπ(r−dc t)). Circle orthogonality and ∫₀¹sin²(πt)dt=∫₀¹cos²(πt)dt=1/2 give

  Q(η_k)=nπ²/2 [1−d(d+1)c²k²/2].

The mixed Hessian between two distinct modes is zero, again by circle orthogonality at each t. For all sufficiently large k the displayed number is negative. The linear span of these modes, with finite sums understood, is an infinite-dimensional negative subspace of the full smooth Hessian. Every fixed finite combination gives a legitimate strictly positive spatial path for sufficiently small ε, because the unperturbed form h is uniformly positive and all its perturbation derivatives are bounded on the compact domain. Since the first variation vanishes, any one negative direction lowers action for small nonzero ε. This disproves local minimization in the smooth full-X positive path class, even in its smooth topology.

Here is the exact n=3, c=1 example. Define

  f_ε(t,r)=t+ε sin(πt)cos(π(r−2t)).

It has global descent and the same endpoints. Writing A=sin(πt), C=cos(πt), θ=π(r−2t), its derivatives are

  η_t=πC cosθ+2πA sinθ,
  η_r=−πA sinθ,   η_rr=−π²A cosθ.

For ε=1/100 the positivity bounds are 1+εη_r≥1−π/100>0 and 1+εη_rr≥1−π²/100>0. For d=2 the action is three times the time integral of the circle average of

  (1+εη_t)²(1+εη_r)²(1+εη_rr).

The odd powers of ε vanish by the half-turn θ→θ+π. The second-power time-integrated coefficient is −π²/2 before multiplying by three. For the fourth-power coefficient, circle averaging gives

  (π⁴/8)(C²A²+12A⁴)+(3π⁵/4)CA³.

Its time integral is 37π⁴/64, using ∫C²A²dt=1/8, ∫A⁴dt=3/8 and ∫CA³dt=0. No higher even degree occurs, since the integrand has degree five in ε. Thus the exact action is

  S_X(f_ε)=3−(3π²/2)ε²+(111π⁴/64)ε⁴.

At ε=1/100 it is 2.99852124877875922<3. For the explicit ε=1/100 example the certified action bound gives L_raw≤√(2S_X)=approximately 2.44888597071352394<√6≈2.44948974278317810. These are action-based length bounds, not a numerical integration of the exact length.

The radial competitors need not be strip subgeodesics and are nonbasic.
